newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria slightly cuts pound rate against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Syria slightly cuts pound rate against dollar.

text.p: Syria on Thursday slightly devalued the official exchange rate of the Syrian pound, fixed for years at 42 pounds to the U.S. dollar, to encourage a shift from the black market into the official market, financial sources said.

Syrian banks, all owned and operated by the government, will apply a dollar rate of 43.5 pounds for buying and 44 pounds for selling. The previous rate was 42 pounds for buying and 43 pounds for selling.

Financial sources said the adjustment of the so-called "encouragement" or parallel rate that covers over 80 percent of dealings, was aimed at narrowing the gap with the black market rate which ranges between 48 and 50 pounds to a dollar.
They said the new adjustment, which leaves little margin between buying and selling, was also aimed at allowing exporters to earn more when they change their hard currency at banks.
Under existing law, exporters can retain 75 percent of their hard currency earnings to finance their operations but the rest must be changed into Syrian pounds.

The sources said Economy and Foreign Trade Minister Mohammed Imadi had issued a decree allowing banks to pay interest to Syrian business clients who deposit their hard currency earnings from export-import operations for at least three months. Interest, at a rate of five percent, will be paid in hard currency.
The new measure follows Wednesday's government decision to ease currency regulations and allow citizens to deal more freely in hard currencies without having to reveal the source of their funds.
Economic sources said the moves were part of the country's efforts to reform the economy which has adopted socialist policies for years.
They said the government still intended to proceed with its plan to unify the various exchange rates of the pound into one rate which will be applied to all types of dealings.

This will eventually include the official rate of 11.2 pounds to a dollar which is being used for a very limited number of transactions, and the customs rate of 23 pounds to a dollar which is used to calculate customs duties.
